chunks: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Abu al-Abbas ibn al-Mughira said: He narrated to us al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked, 'Does the woman lead the women?' He said, 'No, except over the deceased. If no one is more entitled [to lead] than her, she stands in the middle with them in the row, and she says Takbir and they say Takbir.'

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased (specifically in funeral prayer context)

ai.seo_question: Does a woman lead other women in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the jurist clarifies that while women do not generally lead other women in congregational prayer, they may do so for the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit) when no male relative or more entitled person is present. The Imam specifies the physical arrangement, noting that the leading woman stands in the center of the row rather than at the front, distinguishing this practice from the male-led congregational prayer structure. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding female leadership in specific ritual contexts based on necessity and entitlement.
